hero.label: About
hero.title: Intrface is about building the most human interfaces solving the most worthwhile problems.
hero.lead: Based in Vrsar, Istria. Working across the EU.

person.label: Founder
person.name: Alex Bašić
body: I have done a ton of things, and most of them came down to the same one: fixing the part of a system that had not made sense for years.
Someone worked around it once, then everyone did, and the workaround became the process.
I like finding that part and taking it out.
That is why the studio builds interfaces — the interface is where a system either makes sense or does not.
I work from Vrsar, on the coast of Istria.

manifesto.title: Intrface Manifesto
open: We do not build websites people have to understand before they can use them.
We build interfaces to the world.
manifesto.first: The interface comes first. The account is optional. The explanation comes through use.
manifesto.arrive: A person should arrive at the thing they came for: the map, the place, the service, the report, the network, the case, the action. Not a homepage explaining the product. Not a funnel. Not an onboarding ceremony.
questions: What am I trying to do?
manifesto.identity: Identity should appear only when it creates value: saving, contributing, synchronizing, authorizing or taking responsibility. An account is a convenience, not an entrance fee.
manifesto.public: The public side should be effortless. Complexity belongs behind the interface, with the institutions and systems responsible for operating it.
manifesto.adapt: We do not ask people to adapt to software. Software should adapt to the situation they are already in.
examples: A QR code should open the place.
A civic report should become a permanent case.
A network should reveal the people within it.
A public service should begin with the need, not the bureaucracy.
layers: Intrface is not about putting another layer between people and the world.
It is about removing the layers already there.
close: The world is what it interfaces with.

close.title: If something in your system stopped making sense, tell us about it.

content.title: Responsibility for content
content.body: {siteName} is responsible for the content published on {host}. We write it ourselves and keep it current to the best of our knowledge. Descriptions of our own software state what is live, what is a demonstration, and what is not built yet.

links.title: External links
links.body: This site links to pages operated by other people — repositories, client sites, third-party services. Their operators are responsible for what those pages contain. We check a link when we add it; we cannot check it continuously. Tell us at <mail>{email}</mail> if one is broken or wrong and we will remove or correct it.

copyright.title: Copyright
copyright.body: Text, images, and code published on this site belong to {siteName} unless another owner is named. Quote us with a source link. Ask before reproducing a page in full.

form.title: The contact form
form.body: The form on our <link>contact section</link> submits the name, email address, company, topic, and message you type. We store that submission and send it to ourselves by email so we can answer you — answering you is the whole legal basis (GDPR Art. 6(1)(b): steps you asked us to take before a contract). Three services carry it: Vercel serves this site and runs the form, Resend delivers the email, and Google Workspace holds our inbox. We keep a message as long as the conversation it belongs to, then delete it. We do not use it for anything else and we do not sell it. Ask us to delete your message at hello@intrface.eu and we will.

ContactForm.messageLabel: What is hard to understand, slow to operate, or difficult to trust?
ContactForm.sentBody: It landed with us. The reply comes from {email}, within one working day.
ContactForm.fallbackFailed: We could not store the message just now.
ContactForm.fallbackMailClient: This form hands the message to your mail app.
ContactForm.fallbackTail: Your mail app should have opened with everything filled in. If it did not, send it to <mail>{email}</mail>.
ContactForm.errorEmail: We need an address we can reply to.
ContactForm.errorMessage: A sentence or two about the system is enough.

index.line: The things you save, read, filed and connected.

IndexAbout.title: The things you save, read, filed and connected.
IndexAbout.lede: Send Index links, videos, repositories, posts and screenshots. It reads each one, files it with the others on the same subject and shows you what links to what.
IndexAbout.catalogueAlt: Ink drawing of an open card-catalogue drawer. A photograph, a strip of film, a newspaper clipping, a handwritten note and a phone screenshot are being filed into it.

can.label: What you can do
can.title: Save it once. Find it by subject, by source or by what it links to.
can.lede: Index keeps each thing with the others on the same subject, even when you saved them months apart and from different places.
can.worldsAlt: Ink drawing of a long table with five trays of index cards, each holding one object: a record sleeve, a whisk, a dumbbell, a ribbon cable and an architectural drawing. A magnifying glass rests on a card in front.

worlds.title: A world for each interest
worlds.copy: Every item lands in a world: software, music, cooking, research. Make your own for what the starters miss.

links.title: Links between items
links.copy: Items link when they share a topic, a creator, a company or a mention, inside one world or across two.

map.title: A map of your interests
map.copy: See every world side by side, which worlds share items, and what connected this week.

search.title: Search by word or by idea
search.copy: Search reads what is inside each item, so a video turns up for what was said in it.

telegram.title: Capture from Telegram
telegram.copy: Send the Index bot a link, a note, a photo, a voice note or a file. It files it for you.

sort.title: A queue to sort YouTube
sort.copy: Liked videos and playlist songs wait in Sort. Keep or drop each one; anything dropped can come back.

collections.title: Collections
collections.copy: GitHub stars and YouTube playlists arrive as collections and stay in sync. Make your own as well.

how.label: How it works
how.title: You send it. Index reads it. You find it.
how.videoAlt: Ink drawing of a strip of film running into a box of index cards held by a paper band, with an hourglass beside it.

send.title: Send it
send.copy: Forward it to the Telegram bot or paste it into the web app. Connect GitHub or YouTube and those saves come in on their own.

read.title: Index reads it
read.copy: It reads the page or the README, gets the transcript of a video and pulls the text out of a screenshot. Then it files the item into a world.

find.title: Find it again
find.copy: Search for it, open the map, or start from one item and follow what it links to.

why.label: Why it holds
why.title: You can see why each item sits where it does.

reasons.title: It shows its reasons
reasons.copy: Each link between two items names what they share: a topic, a creator, a company or a mention.

unsure.title: You settle what it is unsure of
unsure.copy: When Index is not sure where something belongs, the item waits for you under Check guesses. Your answer decides where it goes.

yours.title: Your library stays yours
yours.copy: No analytics, no ads, no trackers. Delete your account in Settings and every item goes with it.

close.title: Index is coming soon.
close.scope: When it opens: invite-only at first, in English, on the web and on Telegram.
